metadata.title: TIMSS 2023 Kortrapport
metadata.venue: Institutt for lærerutdanning og skoleforskning, Universitetet i Oslo

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This short report summarizes selected results from TIMSS 2023 for Norway and, where relevant, compares them with other Nordic countries. TIMSS uses a two-stage cluster sampling design (schools selected first, then intact classes within schools), and the report presents population-representative estimates for student achievement and questionnaire indicators. The manuscript does not specify the exact student weight variable names (e.g., W_FSTUWT) or whether replicate weights (e.g., BRR/jackknife) were applied in the Norwegian analyses; therefore, the weighting approach is not fully documented in this document. For analysts using TIMSS microdata, complex survey weights and replicate weights should be applied to obtain correct standard errors under the TIMSS sampling design, and plausible-value procedures should be used for cognitive achievement scales.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is a descriptive short report that presents TIMSS achievement scale scores and questionnaire distributions/trends rather than training or evaluating a predictive model with explicitly documented plausible-value (PV) and missing-data procedures. PV handling is therefore not applicable as an extractable methodological component from this short report, and the report does not document a specific missing-data strategy for any PV-based estimation. The underlying TIMSS international reporting typically uses PVs and complex survey procedures, but those technical details are not provided here, so missing-data handling cannot be verified from the text.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The report focuses on Norway’s TIMSS 2023 results for two grade targets: grade 5 (barnetrinnet) and grade 9 (ungdomstrinnet). It states that TIMSS draws representative samples by first selecting schools and then selecting intact classes (maximum two classes per school), and that the Norwegian participants comprise 5th-grade students from 160 schools (5301 students) and 9th-grade students from 157 schools (6324 students). No additional analytic filtering (e.g., exclusions for missing questionnaire items, specific subdomains, or task/module completion thresholds) is described in this short report; it presents the available TIMSS results for the specified grade groups.

data.outcome_summary: This TIMSS 2023 short report for Norway provides a descriptive overview of selected results from TIMSS 2023, focusing on mathematics and science for grade 5 (barnetrinnet) and grade 9 (ungdomstrinnet), plus selected questionnaire indicators. TIMSS achievement is reported on fixed international scales (international mean 500, SD 100) with four proficiency levels (advanced, high, intermediate-high, low) and uncertainty is discussed via standard errors; the report notes that differences larger than roughly 7–9 points are typically statistically significant. The sampling design is described as representative with schools selected first and then intact classes, and Norway participated with 5th-grade students from 160 schools and 9th-grade students from 157 schools. The report highlights a significant decline in Norway’s grade 5 mathematics (−12 points) and science (−9 points) from TIMSS 2019 to 2023, while grade 9 results are largely stable. It also reports questionnaire trends indicating a deterioration in school climate (e.g., more bullying weekly and less perceived safety), while emphasizing that TIMSS is not designed to attribute changes to the pandemic or curriculum transition.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is a short descriptive national report summarizing TIMSS 2023 results rather than an empirical ML study. As such, it does not specify an analytic modeling pipeline, PV-combining or missing-data imputation strategy, or any predictive algorithm evaluation; therefore, ML technique fields and structured predictive findings are intentionally left empty. The document does provide sampling and measurement-scale information (e.g., proficiency levels, standard errors, and the grade-specific Norwegian sample sizes), but it defers deeper technical analyses to a later full-form publication.
